subject: STANDARDIZED_INTEGRATION_FACTORY_AND_PORTABLE_OPERATIONAL_TRUST

facts.claim: The standardized integration factory is documented but not implemented.
The architecture is provider-neutral and technology-neutral; no global preferred stack or production provider is selected.
AWS is a replaceable reference validation environment, not a production dependency or mandatory system.
Operational trust preflight is a conditional gate before functional testing when infrastructure, writes, credentials, persistent state, security boundaries, costs or teardown are involved.
M0 inventory and baseline are complete: four current modules, 27 distinct activation signals, six composition rules, one exclusion block and 13 hashed fixtures.
M1 is blocked because the schema and template files currently present are descriptor catalogs; the declared executable schemas, templates and CRITERION_MODULE overlays are not materialized.
No shadow registry, active selector change, runtime resolver, ChatGPT behavior change, stack selection, provider selection, AWS execution or Terraform execution occurred in M0 or M1.
The SSE value-discrimination test is a separate line with authorization 147 granted but not started; it does not unblock M1 and does not authorize SSE activation or integration.

completed_work: Documented schema set, template catalog and migration plan.
Completed M0 inventory and hashed baseline.
Executed M1 validation and recorded the exact executable-artifact gap.

required_resolution: Declare an executable JSON Schema dialect compatible with repository conventions.
Materialize ten common executable schema files.
Create draft-only authorization templates that cannot grant authority automatically.
Generate four isolated current-module package instances with unresolved fields marked explicitly.
Run machine validation and rerun M1 before M2.

pending.note: May be executed only under its frozen brief and does not replace or unblock M1A.

risks: Treating descriptor catalogs as executable schemas or templates.
Starting M2 before M1 passes machine validation.
Coupling the portable standard to AWS or another provider.
Creating a global preferred stack before sufficient cross-project evidence exists.
Mixing the SSE value test with the integration-factory migration and misattributing results.
Interpreting generated artifacts, tests or audits as automatic authorization or integration.
canonical_divergences: CURRENT_STATE.json, PROJECT_STATE.json and registry/index.json remain materially behind the recent 147-152 deltas; the new conversation must resolve recent deltas and applicable records rather than treating their older latest pointers as exhaustive.
Authorization 147 remains GRANTED for a separate SSE test line, while the integration-factory migration line has no authority for M1A or M2.
